messages:
alex: quick sync — we need a final, reproducible bench protocol for comparing replay vs synthetic for KV warmup + quant/ speculative experiments. can we lock this down today? :eyes:

maria: yes. summary of my proposal — run 3 modes: replay (customer traces), synthetic (stateless distribution), and hybrid (synthetic with prefix-level KV hits). measure latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, and quality (eval prompts) per-run. include cold, warm, and steady-state phases.

jon: +1. for KV warmup we should include an explicit prefix generator step before measurement, otherwise tails differ. propose a 30s warmup where we send 50k tokens of repetitive prefixes to populate KV. then a 60s steady window for measurement.

alex: sounds good. one question: how do we make apples-to-apples when batch scheduling differs (continuous batching on runtime vs fixed micro-batches in baseline)?

jon: we add two controls: 1) fixed batch size trace (replay preserves original arrival times) 2) synthetic with controlled arrival (Poisson) to emulate batching distribution. then run the runtime with `--force-batch-size` and `--dynamic-batching` toggles to capture both.

maria: here's a sample CLI we'll use for replay runs: 
```
replay-harness \ 
  --trace-file=/bench/traces/customerA-1k.json \ 
  --kv-warmup-seqs=50000 \ 
  --arrival-model=replay \ 
  --out-dir=/tmp/bench/run1 \ 
```
We'll store raw token-level traces and per-request latencies.

sarah: quick note on quantization experiments — we should tie each quant profile to the same eval prompt set and track per-prompt similarity metrics (e.g., embedding cosine + custom rubric). if we only report token-latency we miss subtle quality regressions.

alex: agreed. what about speculative decoding? i know it saves tokens on avg but can increase p99 if mismatch happens. we need a regression gate.

maria: propose regression gate rules: any candidate profile (quant or speculative) must meet:
- latency: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.05
- quality: mean_eval_score >= baseline_score - 0.02 (2% absolute)
- no prompt in eval set drops > 5% similarity
If a candidate fails any check, block auto-rollout.

jon: add logging hook to capture when speculative fallback occurs. we should report `spec_attempts`, `spec_successes`, `fallback_reasons` per-run. been burned by opaque fallbacks before.

perf-bot: PERF ALERT: recent CI run 2026-03-04T10:22Z detected 8% increase in p95 on `quant-fp8-v2` vs `fp16-prod` on small-context tests. link: https://perf.redwood/ci/8921 :warning:

alex: thanks perf-bot. can we reproduce locally with the replay harness? if yes, run with `--trace-file=ci/small-ctx.json --compare-to=fp16-prod` and capture `--kernel-trace` for kernel selection profiling.

maria: will schedule reproduction now. we'll include kernel selection heatmaps and a per-layer op summary. output artifact names: `kernels.csv`, `latency.tsv`, `eval.json`, `kv-hit-log.tsv`.

sarah: small ask — include the eval prompts that trigger quality regressions in the artifact set so reviewers can inspect responses. also snapshot model weight metadata + quant commit hash.

jon: for apples-to-apples, we should normalize throughput by effective tokens/sec per GPU and per-cost unit. add `cost-normalized-tokens = tokens / (gpu-hours * cost-per-gpu)` to the reporting.

alex: timeline: maria reproduces today, we run the quant/spec bench tomorrow, collect artifacts, then a short async writeup for PM/SRE. if anything fails the regression gate we do manual triage. sound ok? :thumbsup:

maria: on it. kicking off `replay-harness` now. will post logs when done.

perf-bot: JOB STARTED: replay-harness #3245 (user=maria)

jon: small note — don't forget to set `--kv-ttl=0` for the warmup runs so we don't accidentally expire entries during steady-state.

maria: good catch. set in config. bye for now, will update in ~20m.
